theater: 高耶河下游與薩拉察河口

battle.name: 利提亞戰爭
battle.theater: 高耶河下游與薩拉察河口
battle.brief: 公元前229至218年，羅馬共和國在波羅的海南岸向利提亞人用兵：先以二十艘船開進高耶河口，圍攻河心沙洲上的木柵堡壘。卡面的投石機就是羅馬攻城器械車裡扭力驅動的石砲，砸開木柵與土壘，缺口由步兵與船隊合擊攻破。

kit.name: 投石機
kit.history: 把絞盤的勢能換成一塊石頭。攻城從此有了可以計算的破壞力。

countries: 利提亞戰爭發生在公元前229至218年之間，交戰雙方是羅馬共和國與利提亞人。利提亞人（拉丁文作 Livii，拉脫維亞語作 Lībieši）是一個定居在波羅的海南岸、里加灣周邊漁場的部族，語言通常被歸入芬蘭—烏拉爾語族，與北方相鄰的愛沙尼亞語同支；社會以漁、獵、采集為主，兼有少量畜養，技術形態接近濱海采集社會，沒有石築城牆，也沒有常備軍。組織形式是若干首領率領的部族聯盟，記載中留下名字的領袖是國王 Viestards，另有若干首領率眾作戰。羅馬方面是共和國的常備軍：由執政官統率的兩個戰團，加上由二十艘船組成的海軍先遣隊與相應的輔助軍。羅馬並沒有在波羅的海沿岸的屬地，所有部隊與糧秣都得靠海路從義大利亞南端的布倫迪西烏姆運來，橫過亞得里亞海，補給線全在海上。同一時期羅馬在同一片海域還在打第一次伊利里亞戰爭（公元前229至228年），艦隊與使節航線共用，這一點決定了利提亞戰爭的規模：它不是一場傾國遠征，而是沿海海軍行動的延伸。戰力結構也極不對稱——羅馬握有機械、兵甲與海軍，利提亞人握有地形、熟悉度與一支齊整的划槳船隊。
countriesEn: The Livian War was fought between 229 and 218 BC, between the Roman Republic and the Livii. The Livii (Livonian: Lībieši) were a people settled on the southern shore of the Baltic, around the fishing grounds of the Gulf of Riga; their language is usually placed in the Finno-Ugric family, on the same branch as Estonian to the north. Their society rested on fishing, hunting and gathering with a little herding, and their technical level was that of a coastal foraging culture: no stone curtain walls and no professional army. Their organisation was a confederation of clans under several chiefs, the only leader named in the record being the king Viestards, together with other chiefs who brought their bands into the fighting. On the Roman side stood the permanent army of the republic: two consular legions, a naval vanguard of twenty ships, and the auxiliaries that marched with them. Rome held no province on the Baltic coast, so every man, engine and ration had to come by sea from Brundisium at the heel of Italy, across the Adriatic; the supply line lay entirely on the water. In the same years Rome was fighting the First Illyrian War in those very waters, and the fleet and the lines of communication were shared. That fact sets the scale of the Livian War: it was not a national expedition but the extension of a coastal naval operation. The balance of forces was lopsided. Rome held the machines, the armour and the ships, while the Livii held the ground, the local knowledge and a neat force of oared boats.
people: 留下姓名的將領不多，但足以看出這場戰爭分兩批人來打。公元前229年，執政官 Lucius Aemilius Lepidus 率領兩個戰團北進，先行的是百人隊長 Gnaeus Octavius 與副將 Aulus Atilius 帶的二十艘船；這支先遣隊在高耶河口建立營地，擊退了利提亞人的夜襲，執政官主力隨後抵達。利提亞一方被記載下名字的只有國王 Viestards，他率眾抵抗，最後帶著家人與部眾退入沙岸後的松林。公元前218年，戰爭的最後一段交給三位執政官：Publius Cornelius Scipio、Gnaeus Cornelius Scipio Calvus 與 Tiberius Sempronius Gracchus；實際在河口指揮戰鬥的是 L. Cornelius Lentulus 率領的艦隊，步兵與攻城器械則由 Scipio 兄弟調度。也有一個重名的細節值得留意：公元前217年負責西西里海面作戰、在利帕里群島附近敗於迦太基海軍的那位 Gnaeus Octavius，名字與公元前229年的百人隊長相同，古代作家沒有交代兩者是同一人還是父子，多數學者認為後者出自前者，但無法證實。把這場戰爭的文字留下來的是李維，他在《羅馬史》第二十一卷用一段話記下全過程，材料取自更早的編年與其父的著作；因此這段文字既是唯一主源，也是唯一把雙方說法放在一起的文本，後世研究利提亞戰爭幾乎全靠它。
peopleEn: The number of commanders whose names survive is small, but enough to show that the war was fought by two separate groups of men. In 229 BC the consul Lucius Aemilius Lepidus marched north with two legions; ahead of him went the centurion Gnaeus Octavius and the legate Aulus Atilius with twenty ships. That vanguard established a camp at the mouth of the Gauja and threw back a night attack by the Livii, and the consular army followed. On the Livian side only the king Viestards is named, leading his people in resistance and finally withdrawing with his family and his band into the pine woods behind the sandbanks. The last stage of the war fell in 218 BC to three consuls, Publius Cornelius Scipio, Gnaeus Cornelius Scipio Calvus and Tiberius Sempronius Gracchus; the work at the river mouth was in fact done by the fleet under L. Cornelius Lentulus, while the infantry and the siege engines were directed by the Scipio brothers. One duplicated name deserves notice. The Gnaeus Octavius who commanded the Roman fleet against the Carthaginians in Sicilian waters in 217 BC and was defeated near the Lipari islands bears the same name as the centurion of 229 BC; the ancient writers do not say whether these are one man or two, and most scholars take the later officer to be the son of the earlier, but this cannot be proved. The text that preserves the war is Livy's, in the twenty-first book of Ab Urbe Condita, drawing on older annalistic material and on the works of his father. That passage is therefore at once the only principal source and the only text that sets both sides' versions side by side, and virtually all modern work on this war rests on it.
kits: 卡面這件投石機是羅馬的扭力式石砲：以木構機身、鐵件軸與絞盤為骨，把搓緊的牛筋與馬鬃束儲存的勢能，經過長臂與短導軌化成石頭的初速；主臂短，擊發時靠配重、皮帶和一座銅製或木製框架吸收後坐，所以體積不大，可以整體拆卸分件運輸，一輛牛車拉不動時便拆開分運。約在公元前250年前後，這種器械已經進入羅馬的攻城器械車序列；文獻上明確描述這類器械的要晚得多，公元前52年凱撒在阿萊西亞的戰記，以及稍後維特魯維烏斯《建築十卷》第十卷對單臂扭力砲的說明，才是這條技術線最早的清楚文本。在利提亞戰場上，這件兵器要對付的是一種特殊目標。利提亞人的堡壘不是石造城，而是立在河心沙洲與沼澤邊的土木木構：削尖的圓木柵、堆起來的土堤、覆蓋獸皮與枝條的掩體，間以粗大的橡木梁柱。扭力石砲在這裡的用處很單純——拋出的石頭不是要打中某一個人，而是要砸塌柵牆、壓垮土壘、折斷梁柱，把整個障礙打得失去結構；這正是它相對精準的箭砲最有優勢的場合。李維在二十一卷裡沒有點名投石機，他記的是別的器械：一座可以整體移動的木製攻城塔，一座用粗繩或鐵鏈拉起、隨時可以扯回的橋，以及在河口用倒木與鎖鏈攔成的封鎖線；第一次推進時攻城塔被火攻燒毀，羅馬人退下重來。羅馬步兵的裝備仍是老樣式：矩形大盾、重標槍、短劍、鎖子甲、帶頰的青銅頭盔、釘底皮靴；輔助軍提供弓箭手、投石索手與標槍手。海軍那邊有登艦用的 corvus 喙板、艦首撞角、銅釘船殼與標槍手。利提亞人一方是自造的划槳船、木柵與土堤、長矛、弓箭與投石索，靠松脂與瀝青做火把。攻城器械要從海船轉載到牛車，沿海泥灘一到雨季就會陷車，這是後勤上最實在的難處。
kitsEn: The card face shows the Roman torsion stone-thrower. Its frame is timber with iron fittings and a windlass; the potential energy is stored in bundles of twisted sinew and horsehair, and passes through a long arm and a short channel into the speed of a stone. The arm is short and the recoil is absorbed by counterweight, straps and a frame of bronze or wood, so the machine is not bulky and can be taken down and carried in pieces, divided among several carts when a single team cannot pull it. By about 250 BC such engines were already part of the Roman siege train. The clear descriptions of the type come much later: Caesar's account of Alesia in 52 BC, and the description of the single-armed torsion engine in the tenth book of Vitruvius' De architectura, are the earliest texts that set the technical line down in words. On the Livian battlefield the weapon faced an unusual target. The Livian stronghold was not a stone city but a timber-and-earth work raised on a sandbank in the river and along the edge of the marsh: sharpened round-log palisades, heaped-up earth banks, shelters covered with hides and brushwood, bound together with heavy oak beams and posts. The work of a torsion stone-thrower here was plain. The stone was not meant to hit a man but to break the palisade, crush the earth bank and splinter the beams and posts until the whole obstruction lost its structure, and that is exactly the situation in which it had the advantage over the more accurate arrow-shooting engines. Livy does not name the stone-thrower in book twenty-one. What he records are other machines: a movable wooden tower, a bridge hauled on stout ropes or chains that could be pulled back at will, and a barrier of felled trees and chains stretched across the river mouth. In the first attempt the tower was burned by the defenders' fire and the Romans fell back. The Roman infantry carried the usual kit, the rectangular scutum, the heavy pilum, the short gladius, mail armour, a bronze helmet with cheek pieces and boots with nailed soles; the auxiliaries supplied archers, slingers and javelin-men. The navy had the corvus boarding bridge, the bronze ram at the prow, copper-riveted hulls and spear-armed marines. The Livii had their own oared craft, palisades and earth banks, spears, bows and slings, and made torches of resin and pitch. The siege engines had to be transhipped from the ships onto ox-carts, and on coastal mud a single wet spell could bog the whole train down, which was the plainest difficulty on the logistics side.
tactics: 這場戰爭的戰術骨架是海軍登陸加上封鎖，而不是正面會戰。第一段是外交破裂。羅馬派使者到高耶河口岸，要求利提亞人歸還掠走的貨物、停止襲擾商旅、不得越過河界；利提亞王的回應是要求羅馬人退出高耶河，使者被扣下並殺害。羅馬視之為宣戰，公元前229年即派出執政官與兩個戰團。第二段是河口營地的消耗。先遣隊二十艘船先抵高耶河口築營，掘壕、削尖木柵、壘石成牆；利提亞人沒有解營地的能力，改為夜襲，試圖用火把與投石在夜裡製造混亂，羅馬守軍以盾牆和短程反擊把人打退。接著利提亞人放棄自己的城鎮薩拉察，把房屋燒掉，退入森林與沼澤，靠林緣射擊拖住羅馬人。第三段是工程對工程。羅馬人造橋跨越高耶河，把可以整體移動的木製攻城塔推到沙洲堡壘前，用石砲與火攻拆木柵；利提亞人則從林邊放火燒塔架、趁亂反衝，羅馬人屢次退回。最後一段在公元前218年：羅馬艦隊駛入河口，利提亞人把砍倒的樹木與鎖鏈橫在河道上攔截，羅馬人仍以浮台載塔推進，先以弩砲與火矢覆蓋堡壘，再由步卒涉水登陸肉搏。整個過程裡雙方都不求速決：羅馬寧可耗著，等對方糧盡；利提亞人寧可燒城，也不願在曠野上讓羅馬戰團展開。羅馬自己也清楚短板——步兵一旦離船，糧秣全靠船，冬季泥灘陷車、春季海峽起風，遠征的節奏完全由海況決定。另一條線索是同期的第一次伊利里亞戰爭：羅馬在同一片海域對付伊利里亞海盜，兩個戰役共用艦隊與使節航線，利提亞人因此被視為海盜的同類而遭掃蕩；這也解釋了為何這場戰爭在羅馬的編年裡篇幅不大，卻整整佔了十一年。
tacticsEn: The tactical skeleton of this war was a landing by sea followed by blockade, not a set-piece battle. The first stage was a diplomatic rupture. Rome sent envoys to the mouth of the Gauja to demand the return of goods seized in raids, an end to the harassment of traders, and respect for the river as a boundary. The Livian king's answer was that the Romans should withdraw from the Gauja; the envoys were detained and killed. Rome read this as a declaration of war and in 229 BC sent out a consul with two legions. The second stage was a war of attrition at the riverside camp. The vanguard of twenty ships reached the mouth of the Gauja first and built a camp, with ditch, sharpened palisade and a stone-facing to the breastwork. The Livii had no power to relieve it, so they changed to night attacks, trying to raise confusion with torches and slung stones in the dark; the Roman garrison broke them with the shield wall and short counterattacks. Then the Livii gave up their own town of Salaca, burned the houses and withdrew into forest and marsh, holding the Romans off with fire from the edge of the trees. The third stage was engineering against engineering. The Romans bridged the Gauja and pushed the movable wooden tower up to the bank-fort, breaking the palisade with stones and fire; the Livii burned the tower from the treeline and charged in the confusion, and the Romans withdrew more than once. The last stage came in 218 BC: the Roman fleet entered the river mouth, the Livii laid felled trees and chains across the channel to block it, and the Romans advanced towers on floating platforms regardless, first covering the fort with arrow-engines and fire-arrows and then landing infantry for close fighting. Neither side sought a quick decision throughout. Rome preferred to wait and let the enemy's food run out; the Livii preferred to burn their town rather than let the Roman legions deploy in the open. Rome knew its own weakness well enough: once the infantry left the ships, every ration came by sea, winter mud bogged the carts and spring wind in the straits decided the rhythm of the whole expedition. A second thread is the First Illyrian War in the same waters. Rome was policing the Illyrian pirates there at the same time and shared its fleet and its lines of communication with the Livian operation, so the Livii were treated as a species of pirate and swept away accordingly. That is also why the war occupies so little space in the Roman annals even though it ran for eleven years.
data: 可以核的數字不多，逐一列出並標明出處。年份：現代通行分期把利提亞戰爭放在公元前229至218年，李維記於《羅馬史》第二十一卷；也有學者把開戰推早到公元前236年，說法未統一。月份：卡面所標的月份是按「春季開拔」的通行推定，李維只寫季節不寫月份。船數：公元前229年的羅馬先遣艦隊為二十艘，李維在二十一卷二十五節如此記載；同一卷提到利提亞人備有約三十艘划槳船。兵力：執政官的兩個戰團在共和國晚期常按每團四千八百至六千人計，但這是編制上限而非本役實數，出征人數與損失在文獻中沒有留下，不可當作統計。地理：薩拉察河與高耶河都在一百公里上下，前者自東南注入里加灣，後者由東北入海，交戰的沙洲堡壘在高耶河下游、距里加數十公里；從義大利亞的布倫迪西烏姆橫渡亞得里亞海到伊利里亞沿岸，航程數百公里，古代帆船視風向可走數日到數週。後果：李維記錄大批利提亞人被俘並押往羅馬，殘部被改稱 Cives Romani 與 Bergiones，戰後沒有留下任何條約或貢賦的記錄。物資：石彈取自河床與海岸的漂礫，繩索用亞麻與大麻，弩弦用軍用牲畜的筋與馬鬃，糧食是船運的小麥、黑麥、鹹肉與酒。損失的確切數字不可考，李維留下的是形容慘重的詞句而非可用總數；可以推知的是，羅馬方面的減員主要來自海路延誤、陷車與疾病，而不是戰鬥本身。
dataEn: Few numbers can be checked, and they are best given one by one with their source. Dates: the usual modern placing of the Livian War is 229 to 218 BC, with Livy recording it in the twenty-first book of Ab Urbe Condita; some scholars push the opening back to 236 BC, and the question is not settled. Month: the month on the card is a conventional reconstruction from the campaigning season, since Livy gives the season but no month. Ships: the Roman vanguard of 229 BC numbered twenty ships, so recorded by Livy in chapter 25 of book twenty-one; the same chapter speaks of the Livii having some thirty oared boats ready. Numbers of men: the two consular legions of the late republic are commonly reckoned at between four thousand eight hundred and six thousand apiece, but that is the ceiling of the establishment and not the number present in this campaign; the strength sent out and the losses leave no trace in the record and must not be passed off as statistics. Geography: the Salaca and the Gauja are both a little over a hundred kilometres long, the former running into the Gulf of Riga from the south-east and the latter from the north-east, and the bank-fort where the fighting took place lay on the lower Gauja, some tens of kilometres from Riga; from Brundisium at the heel of Italy the crossing of the Adriatic to the Illyrian coast is several hundred kilometres, a passage of days or weeks for an ancient sailing ship depending on the wind. Consequences: Livy records that a large body of the Livii were taken prisoner and carried to Rome, and that the survivors were renamed the Cives Romani and the Bergiones; no treaty and no tribute appear in the record afterwards. Stores: stones for the throwers were taken from the river bed and from beach cobbles, rope was flax and hemp, the bowstrings were sinew and horsehair from the army's own animals, and the food was wheat, rye, salt meat and wine carried by sea. Exact loss figures cannot be established: what Livy leaves are expressions of how severe it was, not usable totals; what can be inferred is that Roman losses came mainly from delay at sea, bogged carts and sickness rather than from the fighting itself.
cause: 打起來有遠因，也有導火線。遠因是航線與生意。琥珀之路把波羅的海的琥珀運到意大利，南段經多瑙河、喀爾巴阡山與亞得里亞海通往北方市場；羅馬的商人、希臘的商人與伊利里亞的同盟者沿這條線北進，利提亞人控制的高耶河口正好卡在波羅的海南岸的入口上，誰控制河口，誰就控制這條航線的終點與貨源。同時羅馬正在亞得里亞海東岸打第一次伊利里亞戰爭，把海盜巢穴一個一個清掉；清到高耶河口時，羅馬人把利提亞人的貿易兼掠奪行為視為海盜事業的自然延伸，於是戰爭目標從剿海盜變成拆掉海盜的老家。導火線是使者的死。羅馬派去的使者要求利提亞人停止騷擾、歸還掠物，並且撤出高耶河；利提亞王的答覆是羅馬人該從河口退走。兩邊的條件正好相反，談判當場破裂，使者被殺，羅馬把這當作宣戰的訊號。還有雙方各自的算盤：羅馬在公元前230年代剛打完第二次馬其頓戰爭，需要震懾北面的部族、把亞得里亞海變成自己的內海，執政官們也需要一場能拿到榮譽與戰利品的戰爭，而利提亞人這種有城寨、有船隊、卻沒有常備軍的部族，正好是看起來打得贏、實際上又不至於引來大戰的目標。利提亞人一方則是在守自己的出入要道：河口是他們的漁場、渡口與通往北方腹地的門戶，羅馬的營地擋在河口，退一步就要失去整條路。於是雙方都在邊界線上試探，最後在使者被殺的那一刻，試探結束。
causeEn: There were remote causes and a spark. The remote cause was the shipping lane and the trade. The amber road carried Baltic amber to Italy, running by the Danube, the Carpathians and the Adriatic to the northern markets; Roman traders, Greek traders and the Roman allies in Illyria moved north along it, and the Gauja mouth held by the Livii sat exactly at the entrance to the southern Baltic shore. Whoever held the mouth held the end of that route and its goods. At the same time Rome was fighting the First Illyrian War on the eastern Adriatic and was clearing out one pirate lair after another; on reaching the Gauja the Romans treated the Livian trading-and-raiding as the natural continuation of the pirate business, and the object of the war shifted from policing pirates to pulling down the pirates' home. The spark was the killing of the envoys. The Roman envoys demanded that the Livii stop their raids, return what they had seized and withdraw from the Gauja; the Livian king's answer was that the Romans should leave the river mouth. The two sets of terms were exact opposites, the negotiation broke down on the spot, the envoys were killed, and Rome took that as a signal of war. Both sides also had their own arithmetic. Rome had just finished the Second Macedonian War in the 230s BC and needed to overawe the tribes to the north and turn the Adriatic into an inland sea; the consuls also needed a war that would bring them honour and booty, and a people like the Livii, with forts and a fleet but no standing army, was a target that looked winnable and was not likely to drag Rome into a general war. The Livii, for their part, were defending their thoroughfare: the river mouth was their fishery, their landing place and their gate to the interior, and with a Roman camp planted across it, one step back meant losing the whole road. So both sides probed along the boundary line, and the probing ended on the day the envoys died.
impact: 這場戰爭的第一個後果很簡單：波羅的海南岸從此沒有一個獨立的利提亞政權。這個部族聯盟作為交戰方在文獻裡消失，其名字被官方用兩個新名稱取代——留在原地者稱 Cives Romani，退入內陸山區者稱 Bergiones。這是羅馬處理邊疆部族的典型做法：拆散編制、重新命名、編入盟邦或附庸的秩序，而不是設省或派常駐總督。利提亞人所擁有的舟具型、漁場位置與渡口價值，一併轉入羅馬的交通網；高耶河口的渡船與航標從此進入亞得里亞海與北方之間的定期航線。第二個後果在技術與制度層面。這是羅馬第一次把成套的攻城器械車（可移動的攻城塔、繩橋、扭力石砲與弩砲、填土的攻城錘）連同海軍戰船一起帶到亞得里亞海以外作戰，而且戰役是靠海路而不是陸路維持的。這套經驗直接餵給了後來的西西里戰役與第二次布匿戰爭——羅馬在二十多年後能從海上遠征西西里、在諾倫圖姆海戰中贏得關鍵的艦隊勝利，戰術與工程素養都有這批北向經驗的底子。第三個後果是造船與海軍編制的擴張。伊利里亞與利提亞兩場戰爭連續考了羅馬的船塢、划槳制度與登艦技術，龐大的戰艦編隊與 corvus 喙板的廣泛使用，都是這段時期磨出來的。最後是記憶：利提亞人的名字留在了里加灣南岸的地名與族群名稱裡，薩拉察與高耶兩條河的名稱沿用至今；他們的木舟與岸上堡壘雖然消失，這場戰爭卻藉李維的記載成了研究羅馬帝國向北推進的關鍵章節之一。還有一層戰略上的教訓：這場戰爭與第一次伊利里亞戰爭一起，顯示公元前230年代羅馬的北向政策是以海軍為骨幹、以工程機械為拳頭的；這條政策在公元前218年第二次布匿戰爭爆發後中斷，北歐方向的經營要等到更往後才重新推動。
impactEn: The first consequence of this war is simple: from that date there was no independent Livian polity left on the southern Baltic shore. The tribal confederation disappears from the record as a belligerent, and its name is replaced officially by two new ones, the Cives Romani for those who stayed and the Bergiones for those driven back into the interior hills. This is the standard Roman way of dealing with a frontier people: break up the organisation, rename it, and fold it into the order of allies and clients, rather than creating a province or posting a permanent governor. The boat types, the position of the fishing grounds and the value of the landing places passed into the Roman communications system, and the ferry and the markers at the Gauja mouth entered the regular sailings between the Adriatic and the north. The second consequence is technical and institutional. This was the first time Rome took a complete siege train, movable towers, rope bridges, torsion stone-throwers and arrow-engines and rams, together with warships, into operations beyond the Adriatic, and it kept the campaign going by sea rather than by land. The experience fed directly into the Sicilian war and the Second Punic War: the ability to mount a sea-borne expedition to Sicily and to win the decisive fleet battle off Ecnomus twenty years later rested in part on this accumulated northern experience of tactics and engineering. The third consequence was the expansion of dockyards and of the naval order. The Illyrian and Livian campaigns in succession tested the Roman shipyards, the rowing system and the technique of boarding, and the large squadron builds and the wide use of the corvus were hammered out in this period. Finally there is memory: the name of the Livii survives in the place names and group names of the southern Gulf of Riga, and the names of the Salaca and the Gauja have lasted to this day. Their boats and their shore forts are gone, but the war, preserved by Livy, has become one of the key chapters for studying the northward reach of the Roman state. There is a strategic lesson as well. The Livian War together with the First Illyrian War shows that the Roman northern policy of the 230s BC rested on a navy as its spine and on siege engineering as its fist, and that policy was interrupted once the Second Punic War broke out in 218 BC; the Baltic flank was not worked again for a long time.
result: 公元前218年，羅馬在最後的攻擊中奪取了高耶河口沙洲上的利提亞堡壘，殘餘的舟隊被摧毀或奪走，利提亞人失去了全部的野戰與守城能力。沒有投降條約，沒有贖金安排，也沒有附庸國的名分；羅馬人直接接管這一段海岸，把被俘的部眾押回羅馬編入市民與附屬體系，殘部則在山地散居，改用新名稱重新編組。從軍事結果看，羅馬是決定性的勝利者，但勝法並非決戰：整場戰爭從公元前229年拖到公元前218年，羅馬人靠的是海軍封鎖、工程攻擊與耐心，等對方在孤立與缺糧中耗盡，再以一次集中的水陸協同攻擊收尾。利提亞人沒有輸在一場會戰裡，而是輸在守不住河口這個支點，也輸在沒有遠征能力、沒有同盟、沒有後備兵源的狀態下，無法與兩個戰團的羅馬長期對峙。這場勝利的邊際效益卻很有限。羅馬沒有在波羅的海沿岸建立行省或設常駐軍，因為這一帶的收益不足以支撐常設編制；商路被打通之後，北方貿易的增長主要歸於私商與盟邦，羅馬只收稅與維持航道秩序，這也是羅馬在北方的典型模式：以軍事行動打開通道，然後以最小的駐軍維持存在。就後續而言，公元前218年第二次布匿戰爭與第二次伊利里亞戰爭同時爆發，羅馬的全部注意力轉向西西里與意大利，利提亞的殘餘勢力得以在山區與海邊慢慢恢復，部族聯盟的名號也沒有真正消失，只是退到記錄的邊緣之外。真正結束這一切的是後來幾十年更強硬的北向政策，那已經是另一段歷史。而就這場戰爭本身而言，留在人們記憶裡的，是羅馬第一次把投石機這類扭力攻城器械帶到波羅的海的沙洲堡壘前，用石頭和火去對付木頭與泥土的做法——那台投石機在文獻裡從未被點名，但它代表的技術，正是羅馬在接下來兩百年裡一再重複的動作。
resultEn: In 218 BC the Romans took the Livian bank-fort on the sandspit at the mouth of the Gauja in their final assault; the remnant of the boat force was destroyed or captured, and the Livii lost every means of fighting in the open or of holding ground. There was no surrender treaty, no ransom and no client state; the Romans simply took over that stretch of coast, carried the prisoners back to Rome to be enrolled among the citizens and the dependent communities, while the survivors dispersed into the hills and were reorganised under the new names. In military terms the result was a decisive Roman success, but the method was not a decisive battle. The war dragged from 229 to 218 BC, and the Romans won by naval blockade, engineering attack and patience, letting the enemy exhaust itself in isolation and want of food before closing with a single concentrated assault by land and water together. The Livii did not lose a pitched engagement; they lost the point of the river mouth they could not hold, and they lost the ability to stand off two Roman legions for long without any means of expedition, any ally and any reserve. The marginal gain of the victory was small. Rome created no province and posted no permanent garrison on the Baltic coast, because the revenue of that shore would not sustain a standing force; once the route was open, most of the growth of northern trade accrued to private merchants and to allied communities, and Rome kept the tolls and the order of the lane. This is the typical Roman pattern in the north: open the passage by force, then maintain a presence with the smallest possible garrison. In what followed, the Second Punic War and the Second Illyrian War broke out together in 218 BC, the whole attention of Rome turned to Sicily and Italy, and the surviving Livian power was able to recover slowly in the hills and along the shore; the name of the confederation did not truly vanish but withdrew beyond the edge of the record. What finally ended it was the harder northern policy of the decades that followed, which belongs to another chapter. As for the war itself, what people remember is that it was the first time Rome brought a torsion siege engine such as the card's stone-thrower up against a timber fort on a Baltic sandspit, using stone and fire against wood and earth. The engine is never named in the sources, but the technique it stands for is the action Rome repeated for the next two hundred years.
